summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Skyline through console and API controls for request logging, redaction toggles, and short-term ephemeral storage. Customer cares about PII redaction, VPC-only storage, KMS-managed keys, and being able to turn off request storage per-route. Consensus: pilot Dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive inference, but need answers on audit logs and retention for telecom-regulated data.
topics: Redaction: PII detection and replace vs redact
Pilot sizing for Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-15 16:30 PDT | Duration: 56m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood SE), Liam (Skyline), Priya (Skyline sec), Diego (Skyline eng), Sara (Skyline procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick agenda — we'll run a 30 minute walkthrough of the Console and API toggles for request storage and redaction, then leave 20 minutes for questions and pilot next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Liam: Yep sounds good. We're particularly interested in how to keep call records out of persistent storage and still get observability.
[00:28] Maya: Great, so I'll share my screen. This is the Console home, note the model routing at top, and under Privacy -> Request Storage you'll see global defaults and per-route overrides.
[00:45] Maya: (screen share) So default is "store-requests: on" for hosted, and you can set route-level to ephemeral, redact, or store-encrypted. You'll also see an API flag so you can toggle at call time.
[01:12] Diego: Quick clarifying — ephemeral means what's in memory only and never written to blob store?
[01:18] Maya: Exactly. Ephemeral keeps KV cache for the call lifecycle if necessary but we don't persist the request payload. We do leave short lived traces for telemetry by default but you can opt to scrub those too.
[01:32] Priya: How does PII redaction work? We need names, phone numbers and IMSI-like identifiers removed.
[01:40] Maya: We have built-in PII detectors — regex + model-assisted detectors. Options are: mask (replace with <REDACTED>), pseudonymize (consistent token per session), or remove. The detection isn't perfect — sometimes telecom IDs get split — so we recommend a small eval set up front.
[02:03] Liam: That's good. Can we bring our own redaction dictionary? We have a list of proprietary prefixes.
[02:10] Maya: Yep you can upload a custom ruleset via the Console or API and we apply it pre-tokenization. We'll show the API call in a bit.
[02:22] Jordan: One callout — customers on Dedicated can also run the redaction preprocessor inside VPC on a customer managed sidecar, if you need absolute control over raw data before it hits any Redwood hosts.
[02:38] Sara: Important for procurement — if data ever leaves our VPC are there controls for key management?
[02:45] Ava: You can bring your own keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via partner. All persisted artifacts, when enabled, are encrypted with your customer key.
[03:03] Priya: For auditability we need immutable audit logs of who toggled storage flags and when.
[03:11] Maya: Console has an Admin Audit page — every config change, policy toggle, and API token issuance is recorded. You can export logs to your SIEM (we show examples for Splunk and Datadog). Those exports can be encrypted in-flight with customer-managed certs.
[03:33] Diego: Do those audit exports contain request payloads?
[03:36] Maya: No, audit exports are metadata-only by default — action, actor, timestamps, and affected resource IDs. Request payloads are not included unless you explicitly enable full-request-logging and route storage.
[03:51] Liam: On the API side, can we set this in the request header per-call? We want to keep default off but enable for debug sessions.
[03:59] Maya: Yes. There's X-Redwood-Store: ephemeral|store-encrypted|redact and X-Redwood-Redaction: mask|pseudonymize|remove. We recommend signed admin tokens for toggles in prod.
[04:15] Priya: How does RBAC map to these toggles? We don't want engineers flipping retention flags.
[04:20] Jordan: RBAC is configurable — you can limit toggle permissions to a "Compliance Admin" role. We support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[04:33] Diego: Is there a programmatic way to rollout toggles across services? We have dozens of routes.
[04:38] Maya: We support policy templates. You can define a policy with route-matching and apply to a service namespace. Also an API to bulk-apply.
[04:52] Liam: Ok show us a demo of the API call for redaction and the console toggle.
[04:58] Maya: (navigates) API quick example — here's a curl snippet: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Store: ephemeral' -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
[05:18] Maya: Note you can include header X-Redwood-Redaction: pseudonymize; the response will have pseudonyms but originals never written.
[05:28] Priya: How about logs from the inference runtime — do they ever include full prompts?
[05:32] Maya: Runtime traces are token-level telemetry we keep for performance troubleshooting. By default these are redacted to token lengths and masked if request storage is off, but SEs can request deeper traces for debugging with a time-limited role.
[05:48] Liam: Any SOC2 artifacts we can review quickly?
[05:52] Jordan: I'll attach SOC2 excerpt and encryption architecture after the call. We'll also include a short screencast of the console toggle flow.
[06:02] Sara: On billing — if we use ephemeral storage and minimal logging, do we still incur same per-token charges?
[06:09] Jordan: Yes token billing is independent of storage choices. Storage affects how long we keep data and who can access it, not token accounting.
[06:18] Diego: Pilot question — we want a Dedicated pool for 2 weeks to validate latency with redaction on. What's the expected delta?
[06:25] Maya: Redaction preproc adds small CPU overhead pre-inference; worst-case tail latency could be +20-40ms depending on sequence length and redaction complexity. For most of your flows I expect under 10-20ms. We'll produce bench numbers in the pilot config.
[06:46] Liam: Are there fallback behaviors if the redaction service errors? We can't be in a state that spills raw PII.
[06:52] Maya: Default is fail-close — if redaction fails and route requires redaction, request returns 500 and no content is stored. You can opt into fail-open for non-sensitive routes.
[07:06] Priya: Good. Can we get an export of all stored requests for a legal hold?
[07:11] Maya: Exports are available, but for legal hold we recommend encrypted exports to your S3 with retention tagging. Those exports are logged in the audit trail.
[07:23] Diego: Any differences for on-prem/private deployment?
[07:26] Jordan: Private installs let you disable outbound telemetry and keep everything inside your air-gapped network. The Console still talks to the control plane unless you go fully air-gapped — we'll map those options in the contract.
[07:44] Liam: Competitors ask for log-based debugging — we want the best of both worlds.
[07:49] Maya: You can enable short TTL storage for debugging — e.g., store for 24 hours with automatic purge — and we have retention policies that will auto-delete.
[08:02] Sara: Procurement note — contract language around data residency and deletion verification will be key.
[08:08] Jordan: Understood; we'll include a deletion attestation process in the doc package.
[08:15] Priya: One more technical — how do you handle multi-tenant models and cross-tenant cache poisoning?
[08:22] Maya: We partition KV caches per-tenant and rotate cache keys per session. Also, Dedicated pools are physically isolated.
[08:31] Diego: Great. Can you show the Optimize recommendations for batching vs latency that respect request storage settings?
[08:36] Ava: (switches tab) In Optimize we surface per-route suggestions. If a route is marked ephemeral, we recommend smaller batch sizes to keep mem overhead low; if storage-encrypted we can recommend slightly larger batches with async writebacks. You can export those recommendations to a CI config.
[09:04] Liam: This is helpful. What are the default retention windows?
[09:09] Maya: Defaults vary by tier — Hosted defaults to 30 days for request metadata and 90 days for stored requests unless you change it. Dedicated/Private can have custom SLAs.
[09:20] Priya: For telecom regulatory reasons we need a max of 7 day retention for certain call types. Can you support that?
[09:26] Jordan: Yes, tiered retention policies are supported — we'll add a policy with route-matching for those call types in the pilot.
[09:34] Diego: Any edge cases on redaction where content is reconstructed in model output? e.g., model regurgitates PII in answers.
[09:42] Maya: We have output filters too — you can apply post-response PII detection and mask in the response pipeline. That can be run synchronously or asynchronously. It's an extra check.
[09:57] Liam: Ok let's talk next steps and responsibilities.
[10:02] Jordan: I'll send the SOC2 excerpt, deletion attestation template, and the pricing sketch by Monday 7/20. Maya will send pilot config with Dedicated sizing and KV cache parameters by 7/22. Priya will share the compliance checklist by 7/21.
[10:18] Priya: We'll review and get legal engaged. Procurement (Sara) will expect a data processing addendum.
[10:25] Sara: Yep.
[10:30] Jordan: Anything else?
[10:33] Liam: One ask — can you include a brief automated script that toggles X-Redwood-Store for our staging environment?
[10:39] Maya: Sure, I'll add a sample script and curl examples to the follow-up package.
[10:45] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and pilot proposal.
[10:50] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional speaker overlap at 03:30-03:40; some product names transcribed as "Rwendwood" in the auto-captions but corrected in notes.
